sentences.en: The colleague who helped me yesterday speaks three languages.
sentences.es: El colega que me ayudó ayer habla tres idiomas.
sentences.prompt: The colleague ___ helped me yesterday speaks three languages. (who / which)
sentences.explanation: Who introduce una oración relativa sobre una persona. Aquí es el sujeto de helped.

sentences.en: She asked me where I had grown up.
sentences.es: Ella me preguntó dónde había crecido.
sentences.prompt: She asked me where I ___ grown up. (have: anterior a la pregunta)
sentences.explanation: En este relato pasado, had grown up sitúa la infancia antes de la pregunta. La pregunta indirecta conserva el orden sujeto + verbo.

sentences.en: I used to drive to work, but now I cycle.
sentences.es: Antes iba al trabajo en auto, pero ahora voy en bicicleta.
sentences.prompt: I ___ to drive to work, but now I cycle. (used / use)
sentences.explanation: Used to + verbo expresa un hábito pasado que ya cambió. No equivale a be used to, estar acostumbrado a algo.

sentences.en: By the time I arrived, the meeting had already started.
sentences.es: Cuando llegué, la reunión ya había comenzado.
sentences.prompt: By the time I arrived, the meeting ___ already started. (had / has)
sentences.explanation: Had started señala la acción anterior a arrived. Las dos acciones se sitúan en un relato pasado.

sentences.en: I would rather stay home than go out tonight.
sentences.es: Preferiría quedarme en casa antes que salir esta noche.
sentences.prompt: I would rather ___ home than go out tonight. (stay)
sentences.explanation: Después de would rather usamos el verbo base sin to. La comparación se introduce con than.

sentences.en: She suggested joining a local photography group.
sentences.es: Ella sugirió unirse a un grupo local de fotografía.
sentences.prompt: She suggested ___ a local photography group. (join)
sentences.explanation: Suggest puede ir seguido de un verbo en -ing: suggested joining. No se usa suggested to join en esta estructura.

sentences.en: The meal was prepared without any dairy products.
sentences.es: La comida se preparó sin ningún producto lácteo.
sentences.prompt: The meal was ___ without any dairy products. (prepare)
sentences.explanation: La pasiva usa be + participio: was prepared. El foco está en la comida, no en quién la preparó.

sentences.en: Although the portions were small, the food was excellent.
sentences.es: Aunque las porciones eran pequeñas, la comida estaba excelente.
sentences.prompt: ___ the portions were small, the food was excellent. (Although / Despite)
sentences.explanation: Although va seguido de una oración con sujeto y verbo. Despite necesitaría una construcción nominal, como despite the small portions.

sentences.en: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the train.
sentences.es: Si hubiera salido antes, habría alcanzado el tren.
sentences.prompt: If I had left earlier, I would ___ caught the train. (have / had)
sentences.explanation: Para imaginar otro resultado pasado usamos if + had + participio y would have + participio. El hecho pasado no cambia.

sentences.en: We had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally arrived.
sentences.es: Llevábamos una hora esperando cuando por fin llegó el autobús.
sentences.prompt: We had been ___ for an hour when the bus finally arrived. (wait)
sentences.explanation: Had been waiting destaca la duración de una actividad anterior a otra acción pasada. Después de been va la forma en -ing en esta estructura.

sentences.en: The flight might have been cancelled because of the storm.
sentences.es: Puede que el vuelo se haya cancelado por la tormenta.
sentences.prompt: The flight might ___ been cancelled because of the storm. (have / has)
sentences.explanation: Might have been + participio expresa una posibilidad sobre un hecho pasado en pasiva. Después de might se usa have, no has.

sentences.en: I wish I had checked the departure time.
sentences.es: Ojalá hubiera revisado la hora de salida.
sentences.prompt: I wish I ___ checked the departure time. (had / have)
sentences.explanation: Wish + pasado perfecto expresa un arrepentimiento sobre el pasado: no comprobé la hora y ahora desearía haberlo hecho.

sentences.en: By Friday, we will have finished the first stage.
sentences.es: Para el viernes, habremos terminado la primera etapa.
sentences.prompt: By Friday, we will ___ finished the first stage. (have / had)
sentences.explanation: Will have + participio sitúa una acción como terminada antes de un momento futuro. By Friday marca ese límite.

sentences.en: We will go ahead unless the weather gets worse.
sentences.es: Seguiremos adelante a menos que empeore el tiempo.
sentences.prompt: We will go ahead ___ the weather gets worse. (unless / despite)
sentences.explanation: Unless introduce una condición equivalente a if not. La condición lleva presente, aunque el resultado se refiera al futuro.

sentences.en: You should have asked for clarification before signing.
sentences.es: Deberías haber pedido una aclaración antes de firmar.
sentences.prompt: You should ___ asked for clarification before signing. (have / had)
sentences.explanation: Should have + participio comenta una acción pasada que habría sido conveniente. No es la misma estructura que un consejo para el presente.

sentences.en: Visitors are required to show identification at reception.
sentences.es: Los visitantes deben mostrar una identificación en recepción.
sentences.prompt: Visitors are ___ to show identification at reception. (require)
sentences.explanation: Are required to + verbo presenta una obligación mediante una construcción pasiva. Required es el participio de require.

sentences.en: The report must be submitted before the deadline.
sentences.es: El informe debe entregarse antes de la fecha límite.
sentences.prompt: The report must ___ submitted before the deadline. (be / been)
sentences.explanation: La pasiva con un modal usa modal + be + participio: must be submitted. Must no va seguido de been directamente.

sentences.en: The manager said that the figures would be reviewed.
sentences.es: La gerente dijo que las cifras se revisarían.
sentences.prompt: The manager said that the figures ___ be reviewed. (would / will: futuro desde un momento pasado)
sentences.explanation: En este relato, would expresa un futuro visto desde el momento pasado de said. Be reviewed mantiene la construcción pasiva.

sentences.en: I have been studying English since I changed jobs.
sentences.es: Estudio inglés desde que cambié de trabajo.
sentences.prompt: I have ___ studying English since I changed jobs. (been / being)
sentences.explanation: Have been + verbo en -ing destaca una actividad que comenzó antes y continúa. Since introduce el momento de inicio.

sentences.en: This is the most useful course I have ever taken.
sentences.es: Este es el curso más útil que he hecho.
sentences.prompt: This is the most useful course I have ever ___. (take)
sentences.explanation: Después de have usamos el participio taken, no el pasado simple took. Ever conecta la comparación con la experiencia hasta ahora.

sentences.en: Despite having little time, she checked every detail.
sentences.es: A pesar de tener poco tiempo, ella revisó cada detalle.
sentences.prompt: Despite ___ little time, she checked every detail. (have)
sentences.explanation: Después de despite puede usarse un sustantivo o una forma en -ing. Having permite expresar la acción sin añadir una oración completa.

sentences.en: The proposal is worth considering, provided that costs remain low.
sentences.es: Vale la pena considerar la propuesta, siempre que los costos sigan siendo bajos.
sentences.prompt: The proposal is worth considering, ___ that costs remain low. (provided / despite)
sentences.explanation: Provided that introduce una condición: la propuesta resulta aceptable solo si se cumple esa condición. No expresa un contraste.

sentences.en: Could you explain why the deadline has been changed?
sentences.es: ¿Podrías explicar por qué se cambió la fecha límite?
sentences.prompt: Could you explain why the deadline has ___ changed? (been / being)
sentences.explanation: Has been changed es una pasiva en presente perfecto. Dentro de la pregunta indirecta, el sujeto aparece antes del verbo.

sentences.en: What I meant was that we needed more evidence.
sentences.es: Lo que quise decir fue que necesitábamos más evidencia.
sentences.prompt: What I ___ was that we needed more evidence. (mean: pasado)
sentences.explanation: Meant es el pasado irregular de mean. What I meant was… permite aclarar la intención de una intervención anterior.

readings.title: Joining a new team
readings.intro: Maya is an engineer. She starts a new job on Monday. Her colleague Sam shows her the office.
readings.text: Maya introduces herself to a new team on Monday. She has worked as an engineer for five years, but this is her first job in a small company. Sam offers to show her around. Maya asks who she should contact when she has a question, rather than pretending that she already knows how everything works.
readings.extension: At her previous workplace, newcomers received a detailed handbook. Here, responsibilities are less clearly divided. Maya initially finds this confusing, although she appreciates being able to speak directly to colleagues. She decides to keep a list of useful contacts and check her understanding after meetings. Her manager welcomes the questions because earlier misunderstandings have delayed projects. Maya concludes that asking for guidance can demonstrate responsibility rather than a lack of ability.

options: Engineer
Teacher
Receptionist
gentle.explanation: El texto dice que Maya es ingeniera.

options: Sam
Maya’s manager
A client
gentle.explanation: Sam es el colega que le muestra la oficina.

standard.prompt: What is new for Maya?
options: Working in a small company
Working as an engineer
Starting a career with no previous experience
standard.explanation: Ya tiene cinco años de experiencia, pero nunca había trabajado en una empresa pequeña.

standard.prompt: Why does Maya ask who to contact?
standard.answer: To know where to get help
options: To know where to get help
To arrange another interview before joining
To find out who will replace Sam
standard.explanation: Pregunta a quién acudir cuando tenga una duda.

challenge.prompt: Which assumption does Maya challenge?
challenge.answer: Asking questions always suggests incompetence
options: Asking questions always suggests incompetence
Experience removes the need for a list of contacts
Direct contact with colleagues prevents confusion
challenge.explanation: La conclusión contrapone pedir orientación con la idea de parecer incapaz.

challenge.prompt: Why is the manager receptive to questions?
challenge.answer: Clarification may prevent delays
options: Clarification may prevent delays
Questions will replace the need to check understanding
Maya needs to explain the handbook to new colleagues
challenge.explanation: Los malentendidos anteriores retrasaron proyectos; aclarar dudas puede evitar que se repitan.

readings.writing: Present a professional or personal change. Explain two difficulties, how you would respond, and why asking for help can be useful.

readings.title: A different commute
readings.intro: Luis goes to work by bus. The trip takes thirty minutes. On Fridays, he works at home.
readings.text: Luis used to drive to the office every day. Now he takes the bus four days a week and works from home on Fridays. The bus journey takes thirty minutes, ten minutes longer than driving. However, he can read on the way and no longer has to pay for parking. He thinks the change is worthwhile.
readings.extension: The arrangement is not perfect: services are less frequent in the evening, so staying late can mean a long wait. Luis has discussed this with his team and now schedules most meetings before four. He knows that colleagues who live outside the bus network may not have the same choice. For that reason, he supports flexible working arrangements rather than a rule requiring everyone to use public transport.

gentle.prompt: How does Luis travel to work?
options: By bus
By train
By bicycle
gentle.explanation: El texto indica que Luis va en autobús.

gentle.prompt: Where does he work on Fridays?
options: At home
At a station
At a café
gentle.explanation: Los viernes trabaja en casa.

standard.prompt: How long did driving take?
options: Twenty minutes
Thirty minutes
Forty minutes
standard.explanation: El autobús tarda treinta minutos, diez más que el auto: antes tardaba veinte.

standard.prompt: Which benefit does Luis mention?
options: He saves money on parking
He arrives ten minutes earlier
He works at home four days a week
standard.explanation: Ya no paga estacionamiento; el trayecto es más largo, no más corto.

challenge.prompt: Why does Luis prefer flexibility to a compulsory rule?
challenge.answer: Not everyone has access to the same transport
options: Not everyone has access to the same transport
The team has agreed to work from home every day
The bus is faster than driving for all his colleagues
challenge.explanation: Reconoce que algunos colegas viven fuera de la red de autobuses.

challenge.prompt: What does changing meeting times address?
challenge.answer: The reduced evening service
options: The reduced evening service
The longer journey in the morning
The need to work from home on Fridays
challenge.explanation: Programar reuniones antes de las cuatro reduce el riesgo de esperar mucho al salir tarde.

readings.writing: Compare two ways of travelling or organising your day. Recommend one while acknowledging a situation in which the other would work better.

readings.title: The photography group
readings.intro: A local photography group meets on Saturdays. Members take photos in the park. New members can use a phone.
readings.text: A photography group invites new members to its Saturday walks. Expensive equipment is not required; a phone is enough. Each walk has a theme, such as light or movement. Afterwards, members choose one photograph and explain their choice. The organiser says that discussing an ordinary image carefully can be more useful than taking hundreds of pictures without looking at them again.
readings.extension: Some experienced members initially wanted separate walks for beginners. Others argued that mixed groups allow people to learn from different perspectives. The group agreed to keep the walks open to everyone while offering optional technical sessions afterwards. Attendance has increased, but the organiser cautions that numbers alone do not show whether people are learning. She also collects examples of how members explain changes in their work.

options: On Saturdays
On Mondays
Every evening
gentle.explanation: Las reuniones son los sábados.

gentle.prompt: Can a new member use a phone?
options: Yes
Only after buying a camera
Only at home
gentle.explanation: El texto dice que los nuevos miembros pueden usar un teléfono.

standard.prompt: What happens after a walk?
options: Members discuss a chosen photograph
Members choose a theme for every future walk
Members submit all their pictures without discussion
standard.explanation: Cada persona elige una fotografía y explica su elección.

standard.prompt: What does the organiser value?
options: Reflecting on a photograph
Taking as many photographs as possible
Choosing only unusual subjects
standard.explanation: La explicación compara revisar una imagen con tomar cientos sin volver a mirarlas.

challenge.prompt: What compromise did the group reach?
challenge.answer: Shared walks with optional technical sessions
options: Shared walks with optional technical sessions
Separate walks followed by shared technical sessions
Shared walks with technical sessions required for beginners
challenge.explanation: Mantuvieron los paseos abiertos y añadieron sesiones técnicas opcionales.

challenge.prompt: Why does the organiser collect explanations?
challenge.answer: Attendance alone does not demonstrate learning
options: Attendance alone does not demonstrate learning
She needs to decide who can join the technical sessions
Higher attendance has made it harder to choose a theme
challenge.explanation: Busca evidencia de cambios en el trabajo, además de contar participantes.

readings.writing: Propose an activity for people with different experience levels. Explain how beginners and experienced participants could both benefit.

readings.title: A café changes its menu
readings.intro: The café sells soup and sandwiches. There is a vegetable soup today. Customers order at the counter.
readings.text: A neighbourhood café has introduced a smaller menu. The owner says that preparing fewer dishes helps the kitchen buy fresh ingredients and waste less food. Some regular customers miss their favourite meals, but others welcome the shorter wait. The café still offers a vegetable soup and two sandwiches each day. Customers with allergies are asked to speak to staff before ordering.
readings.extension: After a month, the amount of discarded food has fallen, although the owner cannot yet tell whether the change has increased profit: ingredient prices have risen at the same time. She plans to keep the smaller menu for another month and record both costs and sales. She has also added one rotating special to give returning customers some variety without restoring the entire old menu.

gentle.prompt: What kind of soup is available today?
options: Vegetable soup
Chicken soup
Fish soup
gentle.explanation: La sopa mencionada es de verduras.

options: At the counter
At a bus stop
Online only
gentle.explanation: El texto señala que se pide en el mostrador.

standard.prompt: Why did the café reduce its menu?
standard.answer: To use fresher ingredients and reduce waste
options: To use fresher ingredients and reduce waste
To make room for more dishes each day
To bring back the customers’ favourite meals
standard.explanation: La dueña relaciona menos platos con ingredientes frescos y menos desperdicio.

standard.prompt: What should a customer with an allergy do?
options: Speak to staff before ordering
Choose the vegetable soup without asking
Wait until after eating to tell the staff
standard.explanation: Se pide explícitamente hablar con el personal antes de ordenar.

challenge.prompt: Why is the effect on profit still uncertain?
challenge.answer: Ingredient prices changed too
options: Ingredient prices changed too
The rotating special has replaced all the regular dishes
Lower waste proves that customers are spending more
challenge.explanation: Los precios de los ingredientes aumentaron, lo que impide atribuir el beneficio solo al menú.

challenge.prompt: What is the purpose of the rotating special?
challenge.answer: To add variety without restoring the full menu
options: To add variety without restoring the full menu
To find the dish that should replace the whole menu
To bring back every former dish at the same time
challenge.explanation: Un especial que cambia ofrece variedad sin recuperar todo el menú anterior.

readings.writing: Recommend a menu or service change. Discuss its benefits, one possible disadvantage, and what information would help evaluate the result.

readings.title: A missed connection
readings.intro: Nora visited a friend last weekend. Her train arrived late. Her friend met her at the station.
readings.text: Nora had planned to reach her friend’s town before lunch, but her first train was delayed. By the time she arrived at the connecting station, the next train had left. She called her friend, bought a sandwich, and waited for a later service. Her friend met her at the station in the afternoon, and they changed their plans for the day.
readings.extension: Looking back, Nora realises that she had allowed only ten minutes between trains. The timetable made the journey look convenient, but it left little room for a delay. She does not blame herself for the first train being late; she does think a longer connection would have made the trip less stressful. Next time, she intends to compare the reliability of a route as well as its advertised duration.

options: A friend
Her doctor
A teacher
gentle.explanation: Nora visitó a una amiga o un amigo.

options: At the station
At the airport
At Nora’s office
gentle.explanation: Su amigo o amiga la recibió en la estación.

standard.prompt: Why did Nora miss the connection?
standard.answer: The first train arrived after the connecting train had left
options: The first train arrived after the connecting train had left
She stopped for food before trying to catch the connection
Her friend asked her to take a later service
standard.explanation: La secuencia usa had left para indicar que el segundo tren ya se había ido.

standard.prompt: What did Nora do after calling her friend?
options: She bought food and waited
She met her friend before buying lunch
She returned to the first station to wait
standard.explanation: Compró un sándwich y esperó un servicio posterior.

challenge.prompt: Which distinction does Nora make?
challenge.answer: The delay was outside her control, but the short connection was her choice
options: The delay was outside her control, but the short connection was her choice
The timetable was wrong about when the second train left
Choosing a longer connection would have prevented the first delay
challenge.explanation: Distingue la causa del retraso de su decisión de dejar poco margen.

challenge.prompt: What will she consider next time?
challenge.answer: Reliability as well as journey time
options: Reliability as well as journey time
The advertised duration without allowing time for delays
The length of the visit rather than the connection time
challenge.explanation: Quiere comparar la fiabilidad además de la duración anunciada.

readings.writing: Describe an event that did not go as planned. Separate what you could control from what you could not, and explain what you would change next time.

readings.title: Finding a suitable route
readings.intro: The museum is near the river. Bus 12 stops outside it. The museum closes at six.
readings.text: A visitor asks how to reach the riverside museum. The information officer suggests bus 12, which stops outside the entrance. Walking takes about twenty minutes, but the usual route includes stairs. When the visitor explains that her father has difficulty using stairs, the officer points out a longer, step-free route. The museum closes at six, so they decide to take the bus there and walk back.
readings.extension: The visitor notices that the printed map marks the shortest walking route but does not indicate the steps. She suggests adding accessibility information to future editions. The officer agrees that a route described as convenient may not suit everyone. However, he explains that temporary roadworks can also affect access, so checking current conditions remains important even when a map has been improved.

gentle.prompt: Which bus goes to the museum?
options: Bus 12
Bus 6
Bus 20
gentle.explanation: El autobús indicado es el 12.

options: At six
At twelve
At twenty past six
gentle.explanation: La hora de cierre es las seis.

standard.prompt: Why is the usual walking route unsuitable?
options: It includes stairs
It is longer than the step-free route
The bus stops too far from the entrance
standard.explanation: El padre tiene dificultades con las escaleras de esa ruta.

standard.prompt: How will they travel to the museum?
options: By bus
On foot along the step-free route
On foot using the shorter route
standard.explanation: Deciden ir en autobús y volver caminando.

challenge.prompt: What limitation does the visitor identify in the map?
challenge.answer: It shows distance without enough accessibility information
options: It shows distance without enough accessibility information
It recommends the longer route as the shortest one
It indicates steps but does not show the museum entrance
challenge.explanation: La ruta más corta está marcada, pero las escaleras no.

challenge.prompt: Why is an improved map not sufficient on its own?
challenge.answer: Temporary changes can affect access
options: Temporary changes can affect access
The revised map will leave out the step-free route
The shortest route is always the most accessible one
challenge.explanation: Las obras temporales pueden cambiar las condiciones de acceso.

readings.writing: Explain how you would choose a route for a group with different needs. Discuss distance, accessibility, cost, and changing conditions.

readings.title: Planning an outdoor event
readings.intro: The neighbourhood picnic is on Sunday. It starts at noon in the park. People can bring food to share.
readings.text: Residents are planning a picnic for Sunday at noon. They will use the park if the weather is dry. A nearby hall is available as a backup, but it must be booked by Friday. The organisers want to avoid charging an entrance fee, so they are asking people to bring food and reusable cups. They will announce the final location on Saturday morning.
readings.extension: One organiser suggests waiting until Sunday to decide, since weather forecasts can change. Another points out that volunteers need time to move tables and that some guests will not have internet access during the journey. They agree to make the decision on Saturday and contact those guests by phone. They accept that the decision may not match the eventual weather perfectly, but consider predictable arrangements more useful than a last-minute change.

gentle.prompt: On which day is the picnic?
options: Sunday
Friday
Saturday
gentle.explanation: El picnic es el domingo.

options: Food to share
An entrance ticket
Office equipment
gentle.explanation: Pueden llevar comida para compartir.

standard.prompt: By when must the hall be booked?
options: Friday
Saturday evening
Sunday morning
standard.explanation: El salón debe reservarse como máximo el viernes.

standard.prompt: When will the final location be announced?
options: Saturday morning
Friday morning
Sunday before noon
standard.explanation: Se anunciará el sábado por la mañana.

challenge.prompt: Why do the organisers reject a last-minute decision?
challenge.answer: Volunteers and guests need time to prepare
options: Volunteers and guests need time to prepare
The hall can still be booked at any time on Sunday
A Saturday forecast will be more accurate than a Sunday one
challenge.explanation: El traslado de mesas y la comunicación con invitados necesitan tiempo.

challenge.prompt: What trade-off do they accept?
challenge.answer: A potentially less accurate weather decision in exchange for clearer arrangements
options: A potentially less accurate weather decision in exchange for clearer arrangements
A more accurate forecast in exchange for less preparation time
A later decision in exchange for simpler communication
challenge.explanation: Priorizan la previsibilidad, aunque el clima final pueda ser distinto de lo esperado.

readings.writing: Plan an event with uncertain conditions. Explain your backup plan, when you would decide, and the trade-off between flexibility and reliability.

readings.title: Clarifying instructions
readings.intro: Rosa has a new form to complete. She asks a colleague for help. The colleague explains the first section.
readings.text: Rosa is completing a form for a training course. One instruction asks for a contact address, but does not say whether this should be her home or workplace. Instead of guessing, she asks the coordinator to clarify it. The coordinator explains that either is acceptable as long as Rosa can receive messages there. Rosa then repeats the instruction in her own words to check that she has understood.
readings.extension: The coordinator realises that several applicants may have had the same doubt without mentioning it. He updates the instructions with a short example. Rosa appreciates the change but suggests testing the wording with someone who has never seen the form. Both agree that an explanation can seem obvious to the person who wrote it while remaining unclear to a new reader. They decide to review the other sections as well.

options: A form
A shopping list
A train timetable
gentle.explanation: Rosa está completando un formulario.

gentle.prompt: What does she do when she needs help?
options: She asks a colleague
She throws away the form
She signs without reading
gentle.explanation: Pide ayuda a un colega.

standard.prompt: What is unclear in the instruction?
standard.answer: Which type of address is acceptable
options: Which type of address is acceptable
Whether the course takes place at home or at work
Whether the coordinator can receive messages
standard.explanation: No se especifica si la dirección debe ser de casa o del trabajo.

standard.prompt: Why does Rosa repeat the explanation?
options: To check her understanding
To ask the coordinator to choose an address for her
To change the instruction before completing the form
standard.explanation: Reformular permite comprobar que entendió correctamente.

challenge.prompt: What broader issue does Rosa’s question reveal?
challenge.answer: Other applicants may share an unreported difficulty
options: Other applicants may share an unreported difficulty
Applicants prefer workplace addresses to home addresses
The form requires information that neither address can provide
challenge.explanation: El coordinador reconoce que otros podrían haber tenido la misma duda sin preguntar.

challenge.prompt: Why test the new wording with an unfamiliar reader?
challenge.answer: The writer’s knowledge may hide remaining ambiguity
options: The writer’s knowledge may hide remaining ambiguity
A new example removes any need to review other sections
Someone familiar with the form can represent every new reader
challenge.explanation: Quien redactó la instrucción conoce el contexto y puede pasar por alto lo que falta para un lector nuevo.

readings.writing: Explain how you would clarify an ambiguous instruction politely. Suggest a way to prevent the same misunderstanding for other people.

readings.title: Choosing a work tool
readings.intro: The team needs a new tool. Tool A costs less. Tool B includes training.
readings.text: A team is comparing two tools for managing projects. Tool A has a lower monthly price, while Tool B includes staff training and faster support. The team has little experience with either system. Its manager asks everyone to estimate the time needed to learn each one before making a recommendation. She wants to compare the total cost, not just the subscription price.
readings.extension: During a short trial, experienced staff complete tasks more quickly with Tool A, but new colleagues find Tool B easier to understand. The manager notes that the trial involved only one type of project and should not be treated as proof that either tool is always better. She proposes a second trial using a more complex task and asks the team to record errors as well as speed. A decision will follow once the results have been discussed.

options: Tool A
Tool B
Both cost the same
gentle.explanation: Tool A tiene el precio menor.

options: Training
Free computers
A new office
gentle.explanation: Tool B incluye capacitación.

standard.prompt: What does the manager want to compare?
options: Total cost including learning time
Only the monthly subscription prices
Only the speed of the support service
standard.explanation: Pide estimar el tiempo de aprendizaje para comparar el costo total.

standard.prompt: Why might training matter to this team?
standard.answer: They have little experience with either tool
options: They have little experience with either tool
They already know both tools well
They need to train the tool providers
standard.explanation: El equipo tiene poca experiencia con ambas herramientas.

challenge.prompt: Why does the manager limit the conclusion from the first trial?
challenge.answer: It covered only one kind of task
options: It covered only one kind of task
New colleagues finished every task faster with Tool A
The trial compared subscription prices but no practical tasks
challenge.explanation: Una sola clase de proyecto no permite afirmar que una opción sea siempre mejor.

challenge.prompt: Why record errors in the next trial?
challenge.answer: Speed alone may not reflect effective performance
options: Speed alone may not reflect effective performance
The fastest tool will necessarily produce the fewest errors
Training time matters only when both tools have the same price
challenge.explanation: Una tarea rápida pero llena de errores puede ser menos eficaz; hace falta más de una medida.

readings.writing: Recommend one of two tools or services. Compare cost, ease of use, and reliability, and explain what evidence could change your recommendation.

readings.title: Measuring progress
readings.intro: Eva studies English every week. She has finished three short books. She writes down new expressions.
readings.text: Eva has been studying English for a year. At first, she measured progress by counting completed exercises. Recently, she has started recording short summaries of things she reads. She notices that she can now explain familiar topics with fewer pauses, although she still struggles when a conversation changes direction unexpectedly. She plans to practise with different partners rather than repeating only familiar dialogues.
readings.extension: When Eva compares recordings, she chooses similar tasks so that an easier topic does not create a misleading impression of improvement. She also keeps examples of misunderstandings and asks what caused them. A high practice score encourages her, but she knows that recognising an answer does not necessarily mean she can produce it in conversation. Her next goal is to explain a viewpoint, respond to a disagreement, and clarify an unfamiliar expression without abandoning the conversation.

options: Three short books
Three jobs
A university degree
gentle.explanation: Ha terminado tres libros cortos.

options: New expressions
Bus routes
Food prices
gentle.explanation: Anota expresiones nuevas.

standard.prompt: What still causes difficulty?
options: Unexpected changes in conversation
Retelling every familiar topic
Finishing any written exercise
standard.explanation: Le cuesta cuando la conversación cambia de dirección de forma inesperada.

standard.prompt: What does Eva plan to change?
options: Practise with different partners
Repeat familiar dialogues with the same partner
Measure progress only by counting exercises
standard.explanation: Quiere ampliar los interlocutores y no limitarse a diálogos conocidos.

challenge.prompt: Why compare recordings of similar tasks?
challenge.answer: To reduce the effect of differences in task difficulty
options: To reduce the effect of differences in task difficulty
To select easier topics and increase her practice score
To replace conversations with tasks she can already complete
challenge.explanation: Un tema más fácil podría dar una impresión engañosa de mejora.

challenge.prompt: Which distinction does Eva recognise?
challenge.answer: Recognising an answer differs from producing it spontaneously
options: Recognising an answer differs from producing it spontaneously
Finishing more exercises is enough to handle unexpected replies
Fewer pauses on familiar topics means unfamiliar topics are equally easy
challenge.explanation: El texto distingue reconocimiento y producción en una conversación.

readings.writing: Describe evidence of improvement in a skill. Explain the limits of one measurement and propose a realistic next goal.

readings.title: A library proposal
readings.intro: The library opens at nine. Some residents want it to close later. They want more time to read after work.
readings.text: Residents have proposed extending the library’s evening opening hours. Supporters say this would help people who work during the day. Others are concerned about staffing costs. The library director suggests opening late on two evenings for three months before deciding whether to expand the schedule permanently. She plans to collect attendance figures and comments from visitors.
readings.extension: Some supporters argue that a public service should not be judged only by the number of visitors. A quiet evening may still be valuable to someone who has no other place to study. The director agrees, but notes that staff time is limited and that longer hours could mean reducing another service. She proposes asking visitors what they use the evening sessions for and which alternatives they would have if the library were closed.

options: At nine
At six
At midnight
gentle.explanation: La biblioteca abre a las nueve.

gentle.prompt: Why do some residents want later opening hours?
options: To read after work
To close the library permanently
To avoid reading
gentle.explanation: Quieren disponer de más tiempo después del trabajo.

standard.prompt: What does the director propose initially?
standard.answer: A three-month trial on two evenings
options: A three-month trial on two evenings
A permanent extension beginning on two evenings
A trial on every evening for two months
standard.explanation: Propone probar dos tardes durante tres meses antes de una decisión permanente.

standard.prompt: What concern do some residents raise?
options: Staffing costs
Reduced demand during the day
The length of the trial period
standard.explanation: La preocupación mencionada es el costo del personal.

challenge.prompt: Why might attendance alone be an incomplete measure?
challenge.answer: A small number of visitors may receive substantial benefit
options: A small number of visitors may receive substantial benefit
High attendance would prove that no other service needs funding
The director has decided that comments should replace all attendance data
challenge.explanation: El beneficio para una persona sin otro lugar donde estudiar puede ser importante aunque asista poca gente.

challenge.prompt: What constraint does the director emphasise?
challenge.answer: Extending hours may require reducing another service
options: Extending hours may require reducing another service
The trial requires the library to stop opening during the day
Staffing costs will fall automatically when the library opens later
challenge.explanation: El tiempo del personal es limitado, por lo que ampliar un servicio puede afectar a otro.

readings.writing: Argue for or against a change to a public service. Acknowledge a counterargument and explain what evidence should inform the decision.

readings.title: Reaching an agreement
readings.intro: Two colleagues are planning a presentation. One wants more examples. The other wants a shorter talk.
readings.text: Two colleagues disagree about a presentation. One wants to include more examples, while the other worries that the audience will lose interest if it is too long. Instead of repeating their positions, they ask what the audience needs to understand. They agree to keep two detailed examples in the main talk and provide the remaining information in a separate document.
readings.extension: During rehearsal, they discover that one of the examples takes much longer to explain than expected. Rather than simply speaking faster, they remove background details that are not necessary for the main point. They check with a colleague who is unfamiliar with the project to see whether the explanation still makes sense. Both recognise that agreement on a plan does not remove the need to test it and revise it when new information appears.

options: A presentation
A holiday
A menu
gentle.explanation: Están preparando una presentación.

options: More examples
A different office
A later train
gentle.explanation: Uno quiere incluir más ejemplos.

standard.prompt: What question helps them reach agreement?
standard.answer: What the audience needs to understand
options: What the audience needs to understand
Which colleague has more experience
How many examples they can read out quickly
standard.explanation: Cambian el foco hacia las necesidades del público.

standard.prompt: Where will the additional information go?
options: In a separate document
In a longer version of the spoken presentation
In the introduction to each of the two examples
standard.explanation: Conservan dos ejemplos y entregan el resto en un documento aparte.

challenge.prompt: Why do they consult someone unfamiliar with the project?
challenge.answer: To check whether essential information is still clear
options: To check whether essential information is still clear
To choose which colleague should deliver the presentation
To confirm that removing an example would shorten the talk
challenge.explanation: Un lector o interlocutor nuevo puede detectar información esencial que falte.

challenge.prompt: What does the final sentence imply about agreement?
challenge.answer: A shared plan may still need revision
options: A shared plan may still need revision
Rehearsal should confirm the plan without changing its content
A compromise makes feedback from outsiders unnecessary
challenge.explanation: Llegar a un acuerdo no elimina la necesidad de probarlo y adaptarlo.

readings.writing: Explain a disagreement and propose a compromise. Address the other person’s concern, justify your proposal, and say how you would evaluate it.
